description:
Found 2026-11-14 while building fz-3sy.9; reproduced on develop 13d4783d0 and 135b67da3 (interp, 40 s timeout, never finishes).

    defmodule W do
      defexception [:original]
    end

    def wrap(x) when is_exception(x), do: x
    def wrap(x), do: wrap(%W{original: x})

    def main() do
      IO.inspect(wrap(:a))
    end

Elixir prints %W{original: :a}. In fz the analysis cannot decide the is_exception/1 guard from the type, so the second clause stays reachable for %W{original: atom}, and each self-call has a new, larger argument type (%W{original: %W{original: ...}}): the activations never settle. With the argument typed any it settles at once, because any absorbs the wrap. Seen in the sample as the type calculator (emptiness::map_clause_empty) under AnalyzeActivation jobs with ever new arrows. fz-3sy.9 avoids the shape in Exception.__uncaught__/1 (it decides by pattern and does not call itself); this ticket is the compiler defect. Related shape, different cause: fz-sc8.100.

FOLDED into fz-9zq.1 (2026-11-14, plan /Users/j5n/Workspace/fz-next.html): same climb shape (μX. :a | %W{original: X}); the clash-fold probe compiles it in 0.1s (67 AA) with output %W{original: :a}. Its acceptance moves to fz-9zq.1's reproducer set.
title: A function that calls itself with its argument wrapped in a struct finishes compiling
